column1: qb4-h01|Unanswered procedure-specific risks or alternatives require the responsible procedural clinician before the consent process proceeds.|The client has an unanswered alternatives question before an elective procedure.|A prior conversation has not resolved this client’s risk question.|The current statement conflicts with the existing signed form.

qb4-h02|For infectious pulmonary TB, use airborne controls; a patient mask does not replace a fit-tested respirator for staff entering the room.|Infectious pulmonary TB is suspected, so airborne precautions are indicated.|Necessary transport requires limiting the client’s spread of respiratory particles.|Patient source control and room-entry respiratory protection are different controls.

qb4-h03|Protect the person during a convulsive seizure without restraining movements or placing objects in the mouth; oral intake waits until fully alert.|Help and timing are underway; prevent injury without restraining the client.|The proposed mouth intervention creates injury risk during convulsions.|Convulsions ended, but safe awareness for oral intake has not returned.

qb4-h04|Place an infant on the back for each sleep in a separate firm, flat sleep space with only a fitted sheet.|Routine infant sleep requires a safe position and sleep surface.|The safe placement recommendation applies to naps as well as nighttime.|Correct position and mattress do not make loose objects safe.

qb4-h05|Ask directly and without judgment about suicide when a client gives a concerning cue; reassurance or avoidance does not assess safety.|The statement may indicate thoughts of death and needs direct clarification.|Avoidance is based on a misconception about asking directly.|The client’s words warrant an explicit safety question.

qb4-h06|Follow the prescribed salt and fluid plan while taking lithium; abrupt low-salt diets or dehydration need clinician guidance.|A sudden sodium change can affect lithium handling.|Sweating and reduced intake can disturb the fluid balance relevant to lithium.|Both new changes can affect the conditions under which lithium is used safely.

qb4-h07|Protect the AV fistula arm from routine blood-pressure cuffs, non-dialysis venipuncture and IV placement, and external compression.|A usable alternative is available; protect the dialysis access arm.|The proposed site remains in the dialysis access arm.|External pressure can compromise the access arm.

qb4-h08|When a transfusion reaction is suspected, stop the blood product promptly while initiating assessment and the facility response protocol.|New symptoms arose during the infusion and a reaction is suspected.|New respiratory and skin symptoms require prompt interruption and emergency assessment.|Improvement alone does not authorize restarting a stopped transfusion.

qb4-h09|During gastric tube feeding, maintain prescribed head-of-bed elevation, commonly 30–45 degrees unless contraindicated, alongside the other feeding safety checks.|A safe feeding setup includes positioning as well as placement checks.|The client’s position changed while the feeding continued.|Placement verification and aspiration precautions address different safety needs.

qb4-h10|With a standard prescribed cane plan for a weak leg, hold the cane in the opposite hand; individualized therapy instructions take precedence.|Standard cane support is opposite the weak leg.|The demonstrated hand is on the same side as the weak leg.|The right hand is opposite the leg needing support.
